messages:
Ava (PM): heads up — Acme just escalated: renewal in 45 days, asking for an SLA + dedicated routing by end of Q2. want to know tradeoffs if we fast-track.
Diego (Eng): ack. need clarity: SLA implies infra isolation + SLO targets + priority routing. could be small infra changes or a bigger dedicated-capacity product depending on scale.
Priya (CS): Acme says their execs view this as a checkbox for the enterprise bundle. renewal is high-risk if we don't commit something concrete. they gave a prototype load profile (~500 concurrent inference qps).
Zoe (Sales): they flagged potential $1M ARR expansion on the table if we can meet the SLA.
Marcus (VP Product): okay — classic customer escalation vs roadmap alignment. Ava, do we have a RICE-style estimate for this request?
Ava (PM): rough numbers: Reach = 1 large logo (but huge impact on ACV), Impact = 8/10 on renewal and expansion, Confidence = 60% (uncertainty on engineering effort), Effort = 8 person-weeks (platform + infra). RICE score is noisy but suggests medium priority.
Diego (Eng): 8pw seems optimistic if we need tenant isolation + routing + observability + runbook. also need SLO/alerting and e2e tests. if we build it generic, engineering might double.
Priya (CS): quick option: offer Acme a dedicated capacity pilot (tied to a short-term contract) — isolated pool but run on hosted infra. Gives them SLA-like behavior without full private deployment.
Ava (PM): two alternatives on table: 1) customer-specific carve-out (fast, higher ops cost, not productized) 2) productized Dedicated offering (slower, reusable). We should weigh short-term renewal risk vs long-term platform strategy.
Diego (Eng): also: fallback option is a capability-based routing + priority queueing with strict capacity reservations. That is less invasive than full dedicated pool. Effort estimate: ~5-7pw for routing + quota system, but SLO guarantees will be softer.
Marcus (VP Product): benchmark decision criteria: - Renewal risk & $ impact - Reusability across other enterprise deals - Engineering debt/ops cost - SLA compliance (legal)
Zoe (Sales): we need something we can promise in writing in next 2 weeks for the renewal negotiation. Even a pilot + signed commitment helps.
Ava (PM): propose this sequence: 1) Offer short-term Pilot (dedicated pool on hosted infra + tight routing) -> 2) Run 4-week pilot with measurable SLOs -> 3) If successful, invest in productizing (Dedicated) with roadmap slot next quarter. This reduces churn risk and buys time.
Diego (Eng): I can scope a pilot plan: infra config + routing + monitoring + limited support runbook. estimate 3-4pw to stand up pilot infra + 1pw for docs/runbook. We can reuse components later.
Priya (CS): Acme will take a pilot. ask: what are launch criteria for pilot success?
Ava (PM): pilot launch criteria (proposal): - baseline latency p50/p95 within agreed thresholds under their load pattern - >99.5% availability for pilot window - documented runbook and escalation path - cost delta and ops effort tracked. If met, CS will get commitment for productization talks.
Marcus (VP Product): agree. but capture legal SLA wording with Legal early. Sales: no hard SLA until productized. Pilot language should avoid contractual SLA but show clear SLO targets.
Zoe (Sales): will tell Acme that pilot provides 'near-production isolation' and measurable SLOs; legal will review pilot contract.
Ava (PM): action items: - Diego: deliver pilot scoping doc + effort breakdown by EOD Wed - Priya/Zoe: confirm pilot terms with Acme and get load test schedule - Marcus: confirm go/no-go thresholds for escalation to productize by next Monday
Diego (Eng): taking it. will include effort for quick automation to reuse for Dedicated later.
infra-bot: deploy-plan created: infra/pilots/acme-1753000000 (ephemeral pool)
Priya (CS): thanks — moving to a private thread with Acme to lock calendar.
Ava (PM): thanks everyone. keeping this thread as the single place for product/eng alignment. :thumbsup:
